To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the more interactivity a communication medium provides, the more positive the assessments of the partner and the quality of collaborative work

(a) people who are more interactive with their partners are perceived to be higher in the three partner assessments (i.e., warmth, competence, and trustworthiness) and that (b) people who are perceived as higher in the three assessments tend to have higher-quality relationships.

(1) people who are more interpersonally skilled and who have higher levels of communication satisfaction tend to be more interactive in computer-mediated communication than those who are less skilled and have lower levels of communication satisfaction; (2) interactive computer-mediated communication leads to higher levels of communication effectiveness and higher levels of communication quality, as assessed by the participants in the interaction; (3) interactive computer-mediated interaction leads to higher levels (or lower levels) of perceived communication satisfaction, depending on the nature of the task
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how people communicate with one another and how they manage the information and knowledge they exchange.
the interplay between people's perceptions of their communication partners and the ways in which these perceptions affect the ways in which people communicate.
the processes by which individuals adapt to each other in the course of interaction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the interactivity model is a useful framework for understanding communication processes and outcomes, but that it needs to be further refined to take into account the complexity of human interaction.
the interactivity model is a good model for the study of communication and the quality of collaboration, but it needs more research and more testing in different contexts.
the interactivity model is supported, but not to the extent that it is a complete theory of interpersonal interaction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
it is a model of communication that is based on the assumption that people adapt to each other in their interactions.

we have examined a variety of communication processes, including the use of nonverbal cues, the use of verbal cues, and the use of computer-mediated communication, to see how they affect the quality of collaborative work.
the more we can understand the nature of communication, the more effective and satisfying it can be.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the more interactivity there is between the sender and the receiver of a message, the more the receiver will understand the message.
people are more likely to engage in collaborative activities with others who are perceived to be more similar to themselves.
people who are able to adapt to each other's communicative needs are able to achieve higher quality collaborative work.
